headline: High-risk workspace and tool-use overlap: Windsurf can write, execute, and use MCP while the cheatsheet is non-executing, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf can read workspace files, use MCP, and process clipboard content, so attacker-controlled text from shared files could influence its tool use. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and does not ingest outputs, so the pathway is one-way and not a direct mutual bridge. The shared filesystem makes injection plausible, but not high because no raw web-content parser is shown.
conditions: IF Windsurf reads content from a shared workspace file that contains adversarial instructions
IF the pair is connected through clipboard copy-paste from python-cheatsheet into Windsurf
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based transfer between the agents for this workflow
Keep python-cheatsheet content in a read-only folder
Require manual review before Windsurf acts on any pasted instructions
Use separate workspaces for documentation and coding
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for file-originated instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Windsurf can read workspace files and send data through its model proxy or MCP servers, so any sensitive material in shared files can leave the local environment. python-cheatsheet itself touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network access, so it is not a leakage source, but it can still be a source of copied content. The shared workspace makes leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in Windsurf's workspace
IF Windsurf forwards workspace content to its model proxy or an MCP server
mitigations: Exclude secrets from the shared workspace
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace for Windsurf
Turn off MCP servers for this session
Review files before opening them in Windsurf
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention rules on workspace reads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git modification capability, and its concurrency model shares state via the local filesystem. python-cheatsheet cannot write, so it will not contend, but the pair still creates dangerous overlap if the same directory is used with other instances or external edits. Uncertainty about orchestration locking pushes this to high rather than medium.
conditions: IF Windsurf and another editor instance modify the same workspace directory
IF git state is changed while files are concurrently edited
mitigations: Avoid concurrent edits in the same repository
Pause other Windsurf instances before making changes
Use a branch per task
Commit or stash before switching contexts
requires-engineering: add file-locking or workspace isolation

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf can act on its own outputs via shell, filesystem, git, and MCP, so if it treats copied documentation or generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into commits or commands. python-cheatsheet is a reference source and does not verify Windsurf's actions, so the pair lacks a built-in verification loop. That makes downstream mistakes more severe than medium.
conditions: IF Windsurf uses text copied from python-cheatsheet as authoritative instructions
IF Windsurf executes commands or commits changes based on unverified generated content
mitigations: Require a human check before execution or commit
Cross-check outputs against the original reference page
Disable auto-execute for the session
Use a checklist for command review
requires-engineering: add verification gates before tool actions

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is evidenced in either profile. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and touches no data classes, while Windsurf handles source code and open files with optional BYOK secrets, but the profiles do not show regulated data flows. The other agent is not cited for a specific compliance gap because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is opened in Windsurf
IF organizational policy forbids code or secret material in a third-party editor
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Disable optional secret handling
Use a separate environment for sensitive projects
Review retention settings before opening files
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
